content_units: Current level and constraints suggest a short, high-focus plan:   2.5 hours per day  , with priority on   time management in Reading   and   clear essay structure in Writing  . This plan is designed to improve exam control quickly rather than cover every topic broadly.
Day   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

Day 1   Day 1   Reading timing + Writing Task 2 structure   Reading skimming/scanning drill; 1 timed Reading passage; essay structure lesson; 1 Task 2 intro + outline   Finish 1 passage in time; produce a clear 4-paragraph essay plan

Day 2   Day 2   Reading accuracy + Writing Task 1 structure   2 timed Reading passages; error log review; Task 1 report structure; 1 timed Task 1 response   Improve answer selection speed; write Task 1 in 20 minutes

Day 3   Day 3   Mixed exam simulation + review checkpoints   3-passage Reading section timing strategy; timed Task 2 essay; targeted corrections; final checklist   Complete core tasks under time and identify last weak points
- Read 1 short academic article intro and summarize it in   2 sentences  .
- Goal: switch into formal English quickly.
- Identifying keywords in questions in   5 minutes
- Scanning for names, dates, contrasts, and numbers in   8 minutes
- Note if you read too deeply before looking at the questions.
- Do   1 IELTS Academic Reading passage   in   20 minutes  .
- If over 20 minutes, write exactly which question type slowed you down.
- If accuracy is below   70%  , review why: vocabulary, distractors, or timing.
- Rewrite the question in your own words
- Add 1 example for each body paragraph
- Topic sentences only for both body paragraphs
- Did the intro answer the question directly?
- Does each paragraph have only   one main idea  ?
- Create an   error log   with 3 categories:
Day 2: Reading Accuracy + Writing Task 1 Control
- Write down   2 timing rules   for Reading and   2 structure rules   for Writing.
- For every wrong answer, label the cause:
- Focus on not rereading whole paragraphs.
- Practice selecting only the   main features  , not every detail.
- Did you compare data instead of listing it?
- Add new patterns to your error log.
- Rule: move on if stuck for more than   1 minute  .
- Write one action rule, such as:
- “I will underline keywords before reading options.”
- Write a final   next-step list   of the top 3 weaknesses to continue after the 3-day sprint.
Targeted Tactics for Your Weak Areas
- For Reading,   do not read every word first  ; skim, then hunt for evidence.
- Spend   no more than 1 minute stuck   on one item before moving on.
- In Writing, always   plan before writing  , even if only for 3-5 minutes.
- Use a reliable template for Task 2:
- Avoid adding new ideas in the conclusion.
- Make each paragraph do   one job only  .
